key_insight: This review shows that industrial engineering methods in elderly care are evolving from static optimization toward AI-enabled, dynamic decision support, but most work still focuses on operations rather than patient outcomes.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest care systems could improve efficiency and coordination in home and community elder care, but clinical benefit depends on translating process gains into measurable health outcomes.
method: Thematic review of 30 seminal studies across elderly care operations
Grouped evidence into home healthcare, polypharmacy management, and chronotherapy
Compared modeling trends from deterministic approaches to stochastic and AI-integrated frameworks
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a thematic review of 30 studies and identifies a methodological shift toward dynamic, stochastic, and AI-supported models, but notes limited outcome-level evaluation.
watch_item: A key concern is that operational efficiency improvements may not automatically translate into better clinical outcomes, especially across hospital-to-community transitions.
paper_title: From Operations to Elderly Care Outcomes: A Thematic Review of Industrial Engineering and Decision-Support Approaches
